book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Trend, Volume & Momentum Opportunity
question: Is NSE:GROWW in an actionable Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend, or is ₹223.52 overextended above its key moving averages?

epigraph.quote: Never argue with the tape. Fundamentals tell you what to own; the 30-week moving average and institutional sponsorship tell you when the market agrees with you.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein, Stage Analysis Principle

web_blocks.html: Since its November 2025 listing at ₹95–₹100, GROWW has staged a strong institutional accumulation cycle [21][25]. On the verified November 18, 2026 ledger close of ₹223.52, price sits just 4.23% below its 52-week high of ₹233.40 against a 52-week low of ₹142.11 [21]. GROWW is firmly in Stan Weinstein Stage 2, trading above its 50-DMA (₹197.41), 200-DMA (₹190.53), 10-week EMA (₹202.09), and 30-week SMA (₹198.24) [21]. However, at ₹223.52, the stock is extended +10.60% above its 10-week EMA and +13.23% above its 50-DMA with RSI-14 at 66.07—breaching our +10% and +12% No-FOMO entry ceilings.

web_blocks.title: Institutional Shareholding Shift: Early VCs Out, FIIs and Mutual Funds In

web_blocks.html: Ownership migration in the quarterly shareholding data confirms the Stage 2 tape [22][24]. Between March 2026 and September 2026, FIIs quadrupled their stake from 2.51% to 10.90% [22]. Over the same two quarters, DIIs more than doubled their stake from 5.92% to 12.73% [22]. Meanwhile, pre-IPO venture and public holdings shrank from 62.88% to 48.23% [22][24]. Combined FII+DII ownership surged from 8.43% to 23.63%, absorbing block-deal supply without breaking trend support [22].

Broader Indian market breadth on November 18, 2026 is constructive but selective. The NSE sits in an Uptrend (narrow breadth) with 66.7% of stocks above their 50-DMA and 3–4 distribution days. FIIs were aggressive net cash buyers (+₹5,866.78 crore) against DII selling (-₹3,159.90 crore) [26]. Because GROWW at ₹223.52 sits +13.23% above its 50-DMA (₹197.41), disciplined buyers avoid chasing and stage bids inside ₹201.59–₹216.10, with a hard stop at ₹194.50.

Relative strength over 1-month (+9.27%), 3-month (+9.18%), and 6-month (+16.12%) windows remains solid [21]. GROWW has printed higher weekly lows along its rising 10-week EMA (₹204.66). Up-week volume has consistently outpaced pullback volume, confirming institutional accumulation [21][22].

web_blocks.title: Options & Derivatives Execution Check: Cash Equity Only
paragraphs: Because GROWW is not currently part of the NSE Equity F&O segment (NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID), there are no liquid listed call spreads or LEAPS to structure leveraged convexity. All exposure must be executed strictly in cash equity with predefined position sizing and a hard invalidation stop at ₹194.50.

web_blocks.html: Let us inspect key price levels on the daily and weekly charts [21]. Overhead resistance sits near the 10-day SMA at ₹221.82 and the 52-week high at ₹233.40. A high-volume breakout above ₹233.40 would signal fresh Stage 2 momentum. On the downside, first support sits at Pivot R2 (₹217.51) and the 20-DMA (₹208.86). Major trend support rests at the 10-week EMA (₹204.66) and 30-week SMA (₹198.24).

Volatility sizing is equally important. GROWW has a 14-day ATR of ₹7.49, or 3.41% of its closing price [21]. A tight 4% stop would get triggered by routine weekly noise. Our ₹194.50 stop gives the trade 3.3x ATR of room below the 50-DMA.

book_paragraphs: Once we know what a business is worth, the next question is whether the market's footprint agrees with our thesis. In Chapter 8, you and I look at the tape—not to predict tomorrow's tick, but to avoid buying a falling knife or chasing a parabolic spike.

On November 18, 2026, NSE:GROWW closed at ₹223.52, roughly 6 percent below its 52-week high of ₹233.40 and well above its 52-week low of ₹142.11. Every moving average that matters for a Stage 2 uptrend is aligned in the right order: price sits above the 20-day moving average at ₹208.86, the 50-day at ₹197.41, the 200-day at ₹190.53, the 10-week EMA at ₹202.09, and the 30-week SMA at ₹198.24. Even better, the stock is only 10.6 percent above its 10-week EMA, with daily RSI at a healthy 66.1 and 4-hour RSI cooled to 54.4. That means it is neither broken nor dangerously overextended.

Now look beneath the price bars at who is actually buying the shares. In March 2026, just a few months after the IPO, FIIs owned only 2.51 percent of Groww and DIIs owned 5.92 percent—combined institutional ownership of barely 8.4 percent. Six months later, in the September 2026 shareholding filing, FIIs held 10.90 percent and DIIs held 12.73 percent—23.63 percent combined. Over that same window, early pre-IPO venture funds and public holders sold down from 62.88 percent to 48.23 percent. When early venture backers exit via block deals and global institutions plus domestic mutual funds absorb every share while the stock marches to new highs, that is textbook Stage 2 sponsorship.

What about the broader Indian tape? As of November 18, Nifty sits in an Uptrend with narrow breadth—66.7 percent of tracked stocks above their 50-day moving average and three distribution days on the ledger—while FIIs bought a hefty ₹5,867 crore net in the cash market against ₹3,160 crore of DII selling. That tells us liquidity is supportive, but selectivity matters. For Groww, the cleanest structural support zone sits between ₹201.59 and ₹216.10, anchored by the 20-day moving average and the 10-week EMA around ₹202.09. And our line in the sand is ₹194.50: a weekly or decisive daily break below that level violates both the 50-day and 30-week moving averages and tells us the Stage 2 advance has failed.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Watch Who Catches the Venture Capital Lock-Up Supply
book_callouts.text: Most post-IPO stocks stumble when pre-IPO venture funds sell blocks into the open market. Groww absorbed that supply as FIIs and DIIs nearly tripled their combined stake from 8.4% to 23.6% in two quarters—a rare institutional handoff.

book_subsections.title: Multi-Timeframe Structure (1W / 1D / 4H) and Cash-Only Execution
paragraphs: Zooming across timeframes confirms why patience and precision pay. On the weekly chart, GROWW is riding its rising 10-week EMA (₹204.66) without the 20-to-30 percent vertical extension that precedes violent shakeouts. On the daily chart, the mild 1.82 percent dip on November 18 leaves price hovering just 1.55 percent above the upper edge of our ₹201.59–₹216.10 support shelf. On the 4-hour chart, momentum has reset to neutral (RSI 54.39) right on the 4H 20-EMA (₹219.60). Finally, note that Groww does not yet have listed NSE F&O contracts—so there are no options spreads or LEAPS to structure. You express this strictly through cash equity.

book_subsections.title: Reading Institutional Footprints in the Quarterly Shareholding Ledger
paragraphs: Technical analysis is often dismissed by pure fundamentalists, yet in post-IPO Indian equities it is an indispensable lie detector. After Groww's November 2025 listing, early venture capital investors naturally began trimming multi-bagger stakes through block deals as lock-ups expired. In weaker companies, that supply crushes the stock below its 200-day moving average. In Groww, FIIs quadrupled their stake from 2.51 percent to 10.90 percent and DIIs doubled theirs from 5.92 percent to 12.73 percent between March and September 2026—absorbing every block while keeping the stock cleanly above its rising 10-week EMA at ₹204.66.

book_subsections.title: Why We Respect the ₹194.50 Structural Stop Level
paragraphs: Every Stage 2 advance eventually pauses or fails, and the difference between a disciplined portfolio and a trapped one is knowing in advance where the chart says you are wrong. At ₹194.50, a break would slice cleanly beneath both the 50-day moving average (₹198.38) and the 30-week simple moving average (₹198.24)—the twin pillars of Weinstein's Stage 2 framework—and push below the September/October consolidation shelf.

Notice how clean that geometry is: from our ₹223.52 close, ₹194.50 is an 11.4 percent stop—wide enough to absorb normal 3.4 percent daily ATR noise without getting shaken out by routine pullbacks, yet tight enough to protect our portfolio from a 25 percent Bear Case de-rating to ₹165.

book_subsections.title: Pivot Levels, ATR Volatility, and Volume Confirmation
paragraphs: Let us also check the exact volatility and pivot structure so our entry and stop orders are grounded in market microstructure rather than round-number guesswork. Groww carries a 14-day Average True Range (ATR) of ₹7.49, which equals roughly 3.41 percent of its ₹223.52 share price. That tells us a normal two-day swing can easily move the stock ₹10 to ₹15 without changing the primary trend. Placing a tight 4 or 5 percent stop just below ₹210 would almost guarantee getting stopped out by routine institutional noise.

Instead, by anchoring our support buy zone at ₹201.59 to ₹216.10—spanning the 20-day moving average (₹208.86), the 10-week EMA (₹204.66), and Pivot R1 (₹204.51)—and setting our hard invalidation stop at ₹194.50, we give the stock roughly 3.3 times its daily ATR of breathing room while sitting squarely below the 50-day and 30-week moving averages. On the upside, Pivot R2 at ₹217.51 has already been tested, and clearing the ₹233.40 all-time high opens a clean air pocket toward our ₹270 Base Case.
